goodFirstIssues.title: data: Canonical Station Data Model
goodFirstIssues.body:
### Analysis Name

Canonical Station Data Model

### Research Question

What is the complete, canonical data schema for a rail station in the AAO ecosystem — covering both real stations (with live operational data) and proposed/ghost stations (with advocacy metadata)? This model needs to serve as the single source of truth that all downstream projects (Station Pages, Station Data Collection, Route Mapper) build against.

### Expected Output

A versioned TypeScript type definition file (`station.types.ts`) and a companion JSON Schema (`station.schema.json`) with:
- Full field definitions for real stations
- Full field definitions for proposed/ghost stations
- Shared base type both variants extend from
- Inline documentation for every field
- At least 3 example fixture objects (one real station, one proposed station, one station with crowd-sourced fields populated)
- A short `DATA-MODEL.md` explaining field decisions and versioning policy

### Data Sources

- Amtrak public station list (station codes, names, coordinates, accessibility flags)
- Brightline station data
- GTFS spec (stop_times, stops, routes tables) — for field naming alignment
- IATA/ICAO station code conventions
- Existing AAO project requirements (Station Pages #5, Station Data Collection)

### Primary Output Type

Cleaned Dataset (CSV / GeoJSON)

### Methodology (draft)

1. Audit the fields required by each downstream consumer (Station Pages, Station Data Collection, Route Mapper)
2. Review GTFS `stops.txt` field names as a baseline for real station properties
3. Draft a base `Station` type with shared fields, then `RealStation` and `ProposedStation` subtypes
4. Define the crowd-sourced enrichment overlay (fields that can be updated by Station Data Collection)
5. Write JSON Schema with `required`, `enum`, and format constraints
6. Create fixture files for testing
7. Document field decisions and a versioning/migration policy

### Will this feed other AAO tools?

This is foundational for:
- **Station Pages** (#5) — the page schema maps directly to this model
- **Station Data Collection** — the crowd-sourced submission form fields must match this model
- **Route Mapper** — station nodes in the corridor GeoJSON should reference station codes defined here
- **Amtrak Station Seed Data Script** — the seed script output must conform to this schema

### Disciplines Needed

- [x] Data Analyst / Engineer
- [ ] Researcher
- [ ] Policy Analyst
- [x] Software Developer (for data pipeline or API)
- [x] Technical Writer

### Additional Notes

- Station code scheme: real stations use the Amtrak 3-letter code (e.g. `CMH`, `CLE`, `CIN`); proposed stations that have no Amtrak code yet need a defined convention — suggest `PROPOSED-{CITY_ABBREVIATION}` or similar
- The model should explicitly distinguish `amenities` (verified, slowly-changing) from `crowd_sourced` (frequently-updated, user-contributed) so consumers know which fields to cache aggressively vs. treat as live
- Consider alignment with the OpenTripPlanner / GTFS-Flex stop schema for future interoperability
- Good first issue for a developer or data engineer who wants to understand the whole project ecosystem before picking up a larger task

goodFirstIssues.title: data: Amtrak Station Seed Data Script
goodFirstIssues.body:
### Analysis Name

Amtrak Station Seed Data Script

### Research Question

How do we bootstrap a complete, normalized list of every Amtrak station in the US — including coordinates, accessibility info, state, time zone, and routes served — in a format that conforms to the AAO Station Data Model and can be kept up to date with minimal manual effort?

### Expected Output

A repeatable script (Python or Node.js) and its output artifact:
- `fetch-amtrak-stations.py` (or `.js`) — script that fetches from the Amtrak GTFS feed (or public station list), normalizes fields to the AAO Station Data Model schema, and writes `amtrak-stations.json`
- `amtrak-stations.json` — seed file of all ~500 Amtrak stations, committed to the data repo
- A `README.md` documenting how to re-run the script and what fields are populated vs. left for crowd-sourcing
- A brief data quality report noting any stations with missing coordinates, missing accessibility data, or ambiguous route assignments

### Data Sources

- Amtrak GTFS feed (publicly available at `https://content.amtrak.com/content/gtfs/GTFS.zip`) — `stops.txt`, `routes.txt`, `stop_times.txt`, `trips.txt`
- Amtrak station page HTML (for amenity data not in GTFS, scraped carefully and respectfully)
- Amtrak accessibility guide PDF for ADA flag data
- AAO Station Data Model schema (issue #6) — output must conform

### Primary Output Type

Cleaned Dataset (CSV / GeoJSON)

### Methodology (draft)

1. Download and parse the Amtrak GTFS zip
2. Extract `stops.txt` for station names, codes, coordinates, and accessibility flags
3. Join `routes.txt` + `trips.txt` + `stop_times.txt` to determine which routes serve each station
4. Map GTFS field names to the AAO Station Data Model field names
5. Flag fields that GTFS doesn't provide (parking, amenities, local transit connections) as `null` / crowd-source pending
6. Write normalized output to `amtrak-stations.json`
7. Run validation against `station.schema.json` from the data model
8. Commit seed file and document re-run instructions

### Will this feed other AAO tools?

- **Station Pages** (#5) — this seed file is the starting dataset for every real station page
- **Station Data Collection** — crowd-sourced submissions are layered on top of this baseline
- **Route Mapper** — station nodes for existing Amtrak stops come from this file
- **Station Data Model** (#6) — this script is the first real-world validation of the schema

### Disciplines Needed

- [x] Data Analyst / Engineer
- [ ] Researcher
- [ ] Policy Analyst
- [x] Software Developer (for data pipeline or API)
- [ ] Technical Writer

### Additional Notes

- Dependency: ideally the Station Data Model (#6) is defined first so the output schema is stable, but the script can be prototyped in parallel with placeholder field names
- The Amtrak GTFS is updated periodically — the script should be idempotent and safe to re-run; consider adding a GitHub Actions schedule to re-generate the seed file monthly
- Brightline stations (~10 stations currently) can be added as a second pass once Amtrak is working — Brightline also publishes a GTFS feed
- Watch for GTFS stops that are duplicated (some Amtrak stations have multiple stop entries for different platforms) — deduplicate on station code
- Good first issue for a Python or Node developer comfortable with CSV/JSON data pipelines

goodFirstIssues.title: data: Ohio Hub Corridor Data File (GeoJSON + Station Nodes)
goodFirstIssues.body:
### Analysis Name

Ohio Hub Corridor Data File

### Research Question

What is the complete, structured geographic and service data for the proposed Ohio Hub passenger rail network — station nodes, corridor segments, proposed service frequencies, and connection points — in a format that can be directly consumed by the Route Mapper, Station Pages ghost station features, and other AAO tools?

### Expected Output

A versioned static data package committed to a shared `aao-lab-data` repo (or the planning repo), containing:
- `ohio-hub-stations.json` — each proposed (and real) node on the Ohio Hub network with name, coordinates, Amtrak code (if exists), proposed routes served, and advocacy metadata
- `ohio-hub-corridors.geojson` — LineString features for each corridor segment (e.g. Cleveland–Columbus, Columbus–Cincinnati, Columbus–Dayton) with properties: corridor name, estimated travel time, proposed service frequency, current status (proposed / study / funded / under construction)
- `ohio-hub-metadata.json` — source citations, last-updated date, version, and a brief corridor narrative for each segment
- A `README.md` documenting the data schema, sources, and update process

### Data Sources

- [Ohio Hub Passenger Rail Study](https://www.allaboardohio.org/_files/ugd/903aba_baf6e83ae6cf40cface66843e66c5616.pdf) — primary source for corridor alignments and service frequencies
- Scioto Analysis economic impact report
- FRA (Federal Railroad Administration) corridor planning documents
- Amtrak Long Distance / state-supported route data for existing Ohio stops
- OpenStreetMap rail network geometry for reference alignments
- Ohio DOT statewide rail plan

### Primary Output Type

Cleaned Dataset (CSV / GeoJSON)

### Methodology (draft)

1. Extract station nodes and corridor segments from the Ohio Hub Study
2. Cross-reference with FRA planning documents for alignment details
3. Geocode proposed station locations (Columbus Union Station site, etc.)
4. Build GeoJSON LineStrings tracing each corridor segment
5. Annotate each corridor with service frequency, travel time, and current advocacy status
6. Match existing Amtrak stops (Cleveland, Cincinnati, Toledo) to their Amtrak station codes
7. Define proposed station identifiers for non-existent stations per the Station Data Model schema (#6)
8. Validate geometry in QGIS or Mapbox Studio
9. Publish as static JSON/GeoJSON with a documented schema and version tag

### Will this feed other AAO tools?

- **Route Mapper** — this is the primary input dataset for Ohio corridor visualization
- **Station Pages** (#5) — ghost station pages for Columbus, Dayton, etc. pull their proposed route info from this file
- **Economic Impact Calculator** — corridor segments and station catchment areas feed the ridership and economic models
- **Station Data Model** (#6) — proposed station entries here must conform to the canonical schema

### Disciplines Needed

- [x] Data Analyst / Engineer
- [x] Researcher
- [x] Policy Analyst
- [ ] Software Developer (for data pipeline or API)
- [x] Technical Writer

### Additional Notes

- Corridors to include at minimum: Cleveland–Columbus, Columbus–Cincinnati, Columbus–Dayton, Toledo–Columbus, and the Lake Shore Limited Ohio stops (Toledo–Cleveland)
- Each corridor segment should carry a `status` field with controlled vocabulary: `proposed` | `in-study` | `funded` | `under-construction` | `operational`
- The GeoJSON should be renderable directly in Mapbox GL JS with minimal transformation
- Prior art: check the FRA's High-Speed Rail Corridor map data and the Midwest Regional Rail Initiative shapefiles as reference geometry
- Good first issue for a researcher, policy analyst, or GIS-comfortable data engineer
